authority: candidates listed here passed verify/validate_candidate.py; nothing here is a board entry until a human reviews and submits it
campaign_name: Weight-6 bivariate bicycle codes at n <= 100: can random trinomial pairs beat the cell's seeded bar?

abandon_criterion.note: a candidate whose 400-trial screen reads at or below 8.889 is not deepened at all; one that reads above it goes to the gate, and its ladder is dropped once two fresh-seed rungs agree at a bound below the bar or at 20,000 trials

bar.note: the best kd^2/n among weight-6 entries with n <= 100 (8.889); 98-6-12 at 8.816 is next, both seeded baselines

direction.expected_value: A weight-6 code at n <= 100 above 8.889 would be the first submitted entry to lead the unrestricted weight-6 cell at that size; the cell's two best entries there are seeded literature baselines.
direction.feasibility: n <= 100 is far under BASE_MAX_N (700); bb.py builds a trinomial pair in milliseconds, the 400-trial numpy screen reads a candidate in under a second, and the gate runs in seconds at this size, so the whole campaign fits in minutes on a laptop with no accelerator.
direction.hypothesis: Random trinomial pairs on small tori Z_l x Z_m (n = 2lm <= 100) contain a weight-6 CSS code with kd^2/n above 8.889, the unrestricted weight-6 cell's best at n <= 100.

novelty.against: the bivariate-bicycle family of arXiv:2308.07915 and the board's seeded baselines at n <= 100 (90-8-10, 98-6-12, 84-6-10)
novelty.claim: a trinomial bivariate-bicycle code at n <= 100 with kd^2/n above the cell's best there

direction.what_a_negative_would_teach: That 120 random trinomial pairs at n <= 100 under a 400-trial screen hold nothing above the seeded bar, so the small-torus trinomial space is, at this depth, already covered by the literature's own picks; the next session should spend its budget on larger tori or on four-term polynomials rather than re-sampling here.

negative_results.detail: 120 trinomial pairs with k >= 1 at n in [40, 100], 400 numpy RIS trials each (1673 further draws had k = 0 and were not charged): the best screened kd^2/n was 6.122 at [[98,6,10]] (l=7, m=7) against the bar 8.889 (90-8-10); That 120 random trinomial pairs at n <= 100 under a 400-trial screen hold nothing above the seeded bar, so the small-torus trinomial space is, at this depth, already covered by the literature's own picks; the next session should spend its budget on larger tori or on four-term polynomials rather than re-sampling here.
